$comment: Authored from docs/plan/state-machines/job-lifecycle.md, which stays the reasoning. This file is the binding form. It is NOT generated: several transitions are written in SQL with a variable for the source state (`job_transition(id, v_status, 'cancelled', ...)`), so a generator could only ever produce a partial table, and a partial table that looked complete would be worse than none. What IS mechanical is the other direction -- contracts/tools/generate_v1.py fails CI if the migrations contain a literal from/to pair that is not listed here.
subject: public.requests.status
note: A client never assigns a status. It requests an action; the server runs the machine inside the row lock and returns the new state or a stable error code.

actors.P: provider, or the worker assigned by a business dispatcher
actors.S: system, a worker or a signature-verified webhook

states.name: draft
states.meaning: Being composed, possibly by the AI concierge

states.name: agreed
states.meaning: Both sides agreed a price; awaiting payment start

states.name: paid_held
states.meaning: Funds confirmed and held by the platform

states.name: in_progress
states.meaning: Work under way, after the pickup PIN

states.name: cancelled
states.meaning: Cancelled by a party or by the system; still reaches closed or refunded

states.name: expired
states.meaning: No acceptance within the request TTL

transitions.guard: None. Drafting is allowed before facial verification.
Customer facial verification verified; country live or beta; category allowed; price within guardrails; not self-dealing
First offer created
Counter within the round limit (default 5)
Counter accepted or withdrawn and other offers remain
Offer pending and unexpired; provider still eligible
effects: expire all sibling offers in the same transaction
snapshot commission rate and agreed amount

transitions.guard: Payment initialised server-side; gateway routed by country pack
effects: set the payment TTL, default 15 minutes

transitions.guard: Signature-verified webhook plus a server-side verify call. Never the client: confirm_payment has no grant to any client role.
Payment TTL elapsed, the accepted offer still stands
effects: the customer may start payment again at the same agreed price
transitions.supersedes: docs/plan/state-machines/job-lifecycle.md transition 9 says payment_pending -> negotiating. That was a Phase 1 draft written before the implementation and it is wrong: negotiating means a counter-offer is outstanding, and after an accepted offer none is. private.expire_payments returns the request to agreed. Found by the cross-check in contracts/tools/generate_v1.py on its first run.

transitions.guard: Payment TTL elapsed, no valid offer remains
Provider confirmed, or a dispatcher assigned a verified worker
effects: open the chat and call window
set jobs.assigned_at, which is what opens the provider's read of the request

transitions.guard: Provider online; location granted; not mock location
Within the pickup geofence, or manual with a reason code
Pickup PIN verified server-side, attempt-limited
effects: release the item float if applicable (OD-04)

transitions.guard: Every kind in the category's proof_requirements has enough rows in proofs, and a job with a destination has its delivery PIN verified. Otherwise ERR_PROOF_REQUIRED.
Auto-confirm window elapsed AND the PIN is verified AND proof exists
Dispute window elapsed; no open dispute; payout account verified and name-matched
effects: referral pending to earned to holding

transitions.guard: Payout webhook confirms success
effects: ledger: held_funds to provider_earnings, gateway_fees, platform_revenue, referral_earnings (zero-sum)

transitions.guard: Payout failed or reversed
Ratings window elapsed, or both rated
No acceptance within the request TTL
Any state before paid_held
Cancellation fee by state and elapsed time, from the country pack
Provider-initiated
effects: full refund to the customer, always

transitions.guard: Provider not en route within the start timeout
effects: release the provider with no penalty to the customer

transitions.guard: Within the dispute window
effects: record frozen_from so a withdrawal restores the exact state
open the dispute with an evidence bundle

transitions.guard: Resolved in the provider's favour
Resolved in the customer's favour, full or partial
effects: ledger posting 6a, which recalculates rather than reverses because the job still happened

transitions.guard: Refund confirmed by a gateway webhook
effects: ledger: held_funds to refunds_payable to customer

transitions.guard: Terminal bookkeeping complete

timeouts.on_expiry: offer expires; transition 5 if others remain
transition 17, only with PIN and proof
